title: Fix orbit scene-off flicker from inspected frames
objective: Fix the verified PNG-level flicker and scene-off brightness in orbit collection renders
instructions: Inspector directly inspected examples/flashlight/orbit_collection_output_validation and found: (1) scene_off_flashlight_on frame_0000 mean luma 20.95, frame_0001 127.07, frame_0002 134.47, so the MP4 flicker is present in PNG frames; (2) raw depth .npy and depth viridis are exactly equal across all three lighting conditions, ruling out camera/path jitter; (3) after warm-up, scene_off_flashlight_on remains broadly lit, likely from baked/static/environment lighting or another source not covered by ULightComponentBase disabling; (4) metadata reports always_persist_rendering_state_disabled=false for rgb/depth components in all outputs, so that setter did not take effect. Implement a focused repair in examples/flashlight/run_orbit_collection.py and tests: add no-write warmup/discard captures after camera sensor setup and after light/scene state changes so unstable initial captures are not written as frame_0000; make deterministic capture state setting robust and truthful, trying Unreal Python property names/methods needed for bAlwaysPersistRenderingState and verifying/readback in metadata; add a scene_off_flashlight_off diagnostic/control path or validation helper so we can tell if scene-off still has baked/environment illumination with flashlight disabled; strengthen scene-off disabling for available non-ULight/environment contributors if feasible through existing SPEAR/Unreal APIs without broad architecture changes. Keep user-facing workflow simple. Do not commit.
constraints: Do not commit. Do not push. Keep changes scoped to orbit collection/render QA and tests/docs if needed. Do not modify generated frame outputs except optional new diagnostic artifacts under ignored output paths if needed for validation.

artifacts: scene_off_flashlight_on orbit validation on 2026-07-01 showed PNG-level flicker from initial unstable frames plus residual broad scene illumination likely caused by baked/static/environment lighting not disabled by runtime ULightComponentBase zeroing.

expected_outputs: Builder ResultPacket with changed files, test/validation results, and exact command for user to rerun the fixed render.
definition_of_done: Frame_0000 should no longer be an unstable first capture after render group setup; metadata should no longer falsely claim persistent render state was disabled when it was not; scene-off diagnostics should distinguish runtime light leakage from baked/environment illumination; tests cover the new behavior.
